propertiesMeta.name: gridTemplateColumns
propertiesMeta.description:
Defines the column structure of the grid. The value is a space separated list of column definitions. 
A column definition can be a pixel value (42px), percent value (42%), 'max-value' or 'min-value' for automatic sizing based on the widest or narrowest content in the column or '1fr' for deviding the remaining free space in the grid into fractions. '1fr' means that all free space is given to this column. 
Example: '50px max-content 1fr'

propertiesMeta.name: gridTemplateRows

A row definition can be a pixel value (42px), percent value (42%), 'max-value' or 'min-value' for automatic sizing based on the tallest or shortest content in the row or '1fr' for deviding the remaining free space in the grid into fractions. '1fr' means that all free space is given to this row. 
Example: '50px max-content 1fr'

TcHmi.Controls.System.TcHmiFlexContainer.title: FlexLayout
TcHmi.Controls.System.TcHmiFlexContainer.description: Defines the layout of the flex container.

propertiesMeta.name: flexDirection
flexWrap
propertiesMeta.description:
Defines the wrapping behavior of the flex container. 
With NoWrap, items are laid out in a single line which may cause overflow. 
With Wrap, items will wrap onto multiple lines, from top to bottom.

propertiesMeta.name: justifyContent
propertiesMeta.description:
Defines the alignment along the main axis. 
With Flex-Start, items are packed toward the start of the flex-direction. 
With Flex-End, items are packed toward the end of the flex-direction. 
With Center, items are centered along the line. 
With Space-Between, items are evenly distributed in the line; first item is on the start line, last item on the end line. 
With Space-Around, items are evenly distributed in the line with equal space around them. 
With Space-Evenly, items are distributed so that the spacing between any two items (and the space to the edges) is equal.

propertiesMeta.name: alignItems
propertiesMeta.description:
Defines the alignment of items along the cross axis. 
With Flex-Start, items are aligned toward the start of the cross-axis. 
With Flex-End, items are aligned toward the end of the cross-axis. 
With Center, items are centered along the cross-axis. 
With Baseline, items are aligned such as their baselines align.

propertiesMeta.name: alignContent
propertiesMeta.description:
Defines the alignment of items along the cross axis when wrapping is active. 
With Flex-Start, lines are packed toward the start of the cross-axis. 
With Flex-End, lines are packed toward the end of the cross-axis. 
With Center, lines are centered along the cross-axis. 
With Space-Between, lines are evenly distributed in the cross-axis; first line is on the start line, last line on the end line. 
With Space-Around, lines are evenly distributed in the cross-axis with equal space around them.

propertiesMeta.description: Defines the gap between columns in the flex container. Can be a pixel value (42px), percent value (42%).

propertiesMeta.name: columnGapUnit
propertiesMeta.description: Unit of the column gap.

propertiesMeta.name: rowGap
propertiesMeta.description: Defines the gap between rows in the flex container. Can be a pixel value (42px), percent value (42%).

propertiesMeta.description: Unit of the row gap.

propertiesMeta.name: overflowY

SubstrateMapSelectionList.title: SubstrateMapSelectionList
SubstrateMapSelectionList.description: The current selection as typed entries. Read-only output mirrored from the control; empty when nothing is selected. 'cell' entries additionally carry binQuality and the signed logical mapX / mapY.

kind.description: Discriminates the selected element: an item geometry or a grid cell.

item_id.description: Id of the selected element: the item_id for items, the cell index for grid cells.

status.description: Resolved status / bin string of the selected element, as mapped via StatusColorMapping. Null when there is none - the control emits null for a cell with no bin, and an item whose status does not resolve.

name.description: Name of the selected element, when it has one. Null when there is none - the control emits null for every cell entry (a cell has no name).

user_data.description: Opaque user_data of the selected item, passed through unchanged; null for grid cells.

binQuality.description: Bin quality of a selected cell as the source declared it; present only on 'cell' entries, null when the source declared none. Absent for items.

mapX.description: Signed logical E142 map X of a selected cell. Present only on 'cell' entries when a map frame is known.

mapY.description: Signed logical E142 map Y of a selected cell. Present only on 'cell' entries when a map frame is known.

deviceId.description: Device id of a selected CELL, from a DeviceIdMap overlay entry addressing the same cell. Null when the map carries no DeviceIdMap or that cell has no <Id>. Absent for item entries. NOTE: this is the identifier of the DEVICE, which moves; see `lid` for the identifier of the LOCATION, which does not.

lid.description: Location identifier of a selected CELL, from E142 BinCode/@LID. Null when the map names no location for that cell. Absent for item entries. E142 13.4: 'A location identifier is distinct from the DeviceId ... The location identifier is still present when the device is removed.' - so `lid` names the socket and `deviceId` names whatever is currently in it. Opaque: never trimmed or case-folded, because it is a join key. An EMPTY STRING is a legal zero-length LID and is not the same as null.

fromSubstrateType.description: SubstrateType of the substrate this CELL's device came from (E142 TransferMap/@FromSubstrateType). Null when the map carries no transfer covering this cell. Reported with fromSubstrateId because an id alone is half a key: SubstrateMapKey is (SubstrateType, SubstrateId, LayoutSpecifier), so one document may legitimately carry a Wafer and a TnR with the same id.

fromSubstrateId.description: SubstrateId of the substrate this CELL's device came from - the R2-3 traceability path. Null when no transfer covers this cell. E142 13.9 and R2-3 make TransferMap the substrate-to-substrate traceability mechanism; R2-3.2.2 describes the wafer -> tape-and-reel -> target chain it records. Absent for item entries.

fromX.description: Logical X on the SOURCE substrate (E142 T/@FX). Null when no transfer covers this cell, or when that transfer addressed its source end by identifier rather than by coordinate - each end of a transfer is addressed independently. Exactly one of (fromX, fromY) and fromLid is non-null for a covered cell.

fromY.description: Logical Y on the source substrate (E142 T/@FY). See fromX.

fromLid.description: Location identifier on the SOURCE substrate (E142 T/@FID) - a tape pocket, in the R2-3.2.2 case. Null when no transfer covers this cell, or when that transfer addressed its source end by coordinate.

deviceData.description: Parameter readings for a selected CELL, from a DeviceDataMap overlay. Null when the map carries none or none covers this cell. Each entry has the parameter name, the value rendered for display, and the raw E138 PVSet value. Names join to values BY INDEX (E142 Table 19); an empty name means the document's Parameter list was shorter than its value list.

name.description: Parameter/@Name; empty when the document supplied none.

value.description: The value rendered for a human. '(nil)' for xsi:nil, '(reason: text)' for NoValue, '(a, b)' for a structure, '[a, b]' for an array.

raw.description: The E138 PvValue itself, for a consumer that needs the tree rather than the text.

overlays.description: Every composed overlay's bin for this CELL, base first, in the E142Overlays order. Null when the map is not composed. binCode on this entry remains the BASE overlay's, unchanged. A layer that says nothing about the cell is LISTED with binCode null rather than omitted - omitting would be ambiguous with 'no such overlay'.

mapVersion.description: Overlay/@MapVersion. With mapName this is OverlayKey, so the pair identifies the overlay.

binCode.description: This overlay's bin code for the cell, or null when it names no bin there.

binQuality.description: The bin's declared quality, or null.

SubstrateMapGroupBinCount.title: SubstrateMapGroupBinCount
SubstrateMapGroupBinCount.description: One named bin in a group's histogram.

code.description: The bin code, as the document spells it.

count.description: Cells of the group carrying it.

SubstrateMapGroupSelection.title: SubstrateMapGroupSelection
SubstrateMapGroupSelection.description: A summary of the cells one tap covers on an aggregated map. NEVER a materialized list: a 48x48 group on a 1.5 M map holds about 12 900 cells, and a per-cell selection list of that size is a multi-hundred-millisecond stall on every tap. This is fixed-size - counts, a truncated histogram and a remainder - and cellsInGroup remains available for a caller who genuinely wants the indices.

id.description: The group's lattice-space origin, "col,row". Stable within a render.

corners.description: The group quad's four corners in LATTICE coordinates, in the device order top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. Lattice rather than device, because a device rectangle means nothing once the view has moved.

cellCount.description: Cells in the group, excluding the null bin.

severity.description: The worst severity rank present: 0 none, 1 pass, 2 unknown, 3 fail or worse.

bins.description: The most common bins, descending by count then by code, at most ten. Truncated because Integer2 permits 65 536 codes and an unbounded histogram cannot honor a size budget.

otherCount.description: Cells in bins the histogram did not name. bins + this equals cellCount exactly.

otherBins.description: How many distinct bins the remainder covers.

decorated.description: Whether any cell in the group carries a decoration layer.

SubstrateMapItemSelection.title: SubstrateMapItemSelection
SubstrateMapItemSelection.description: The payload of the .onItemSelected event. Derived from what __raiseSelected BUILDS, not from SelectionList: the event and the SelectedItems attribute are close relatives and not the same shape, and README section 'onItemSelected versus SelectedItems' lists every difference with its reason. The six always-present fields describe the LAST INTERACTED element; the cell fields are present only for kind 'cell'. A payload with itemId null, every other single value null and an empty selection is a CLEAR - under SelectionMode multi an empty click raises one, so a consumer binding this event must expect it.

itemId.description: Id of the last interacted element: the item_id for an item, the row-major cell index for a cell. Null after a clear.

status.description: Effective status of the last interacted element - an item's status resolved through StatusColorMapping, or a cell's canonical bin code (a cell's bin IS its status; the status resolver is an item concern and is deliberately not consulted). Null after a clear, and for an item whose status does not resolve.

name.description: Name of the last interacted item. Always null for a cell - a lattice cell carries no name - and null after a clear.

userData.description: Opaque user_data of the last interacted item, passed through unchanged. Always null for a cell and after a clear. NOTE the spelling: this event says userData, the SelectedItems attribute says user_data.

kind.description: Kind of the last interacted element. A clear reports 'item' with null values, because a clear has no kind of its own and the item shape is the one without cell fields.

selection.description: The full current selection, as identity only. Items in selection order, then cells in selection order. These entries carry NO status, name or user data - the SelectedItems attribute carries those. Grouped by kind because the two kinds live in kind-specific collections, which is what keeps ring-marking membership O(1) for a large cell selection.

itemId.description: Id of this selected element. Spelled itemId here and item_id in the SelectedItems attribute.

column.description: Column of the last interacted CELL, in Row/Column SERIALIZATION indices. Present only for kind 'cell'. The SelectedItems attribute does NOT carry column or row - it identifies a cell by its linear item_id.

row.description: Row of the last interacted cell, in serialization indices. Present only for kind 'cell'. See column.

binCode.description: Canonical bin code of the last interacted cell, or null when it has no bin. Equal to this payload's status, repeated under its own name so a consumer need not know that. Present only for kind 'cell'; the SelectedItems attribute omits it for the same reason - there, status IS the bin code.

binQuality.description: Bin quality of the last interacted cell as the source declared it (a FREE string, not an enumeration), null when the source declared none. Present only for kind 'cell'.

mapX.description: Signed logical E142 map X of the last interacted cell, null when no map frame is known. Present only for kind 'cell'. On this event the field is present-and-null when unknown; in a SelectedItems entry it is ABSENT when unknown.

mapY.description: Signed logical E142 map Y of the last interacted cell. See mapX.

deviceId.description: Device id of the last interacted CELL, from a DeviceIdMap overlay. Null when the map carries none or that cell has no Id. This is the identifier of the DEVICE, which moves; see lid for the identifier of the LOCATION, which does not.

lid.description: Location identifier of the last interacted CELL, from E142 BinCode/@LID. Null when the map names no location for that cell. E142 13.4 makes it distinct from the DeviceId and it survives the device being removed, so lid names the socket and deviceId names whatever is in it. Opaque: never trimmed or case-folded, because it is a join key. An EMPTY STRING is a legal zero-length LID and is not null.

fromSubstrateType.description: SubstrateType of the substrate this cell's device came from (E142 TransferMap/@FromSubstrateType). Null when no transfer covers the cell. Reported with fromSubstrateId because an id alone is half a key: SubstrateMapKey is (SubstrateType, SubstrateId, LayoutSpecifier).

fromSubstrateId.description: SubstrateId of the substrate this cell's device came from - the R2-3 traceability path. Null when no transfer covers the cell.

fromX.description: Logical X on the SOURCE substrate (E142 T/@FX). Null when no transfer covers the cell, or when that transfer addressed its source end by identifier rather than coordinate. Exactly one of (fromX, fromY) and fromLid is non-null for a covered cell.

fromY.description: Logical Y on the source substrate (E142 T/@FY). See fromX.

fromLid.description: Location identifier on the SOURCE substrate (E142 T/@FID) - a tape pocket, in the R2-3.2.2 case. Null when no transfer covers the cell, or when that transfer addressed its source end by coordinate.

deviceData.description: Parameter readings for the last interacted CELL, from a DeviceDataMap overlay. Null when the map carries none or none covers the cell. Names join to values BY INDEX (E142 Table 19); an empty name means the document's Parameter list was shorter than its value list. THIS EVENT DROPS the raw E138 PvValue that a SelectedItems entry keeps - see the README section for why the two differ here.

name.description: Parameter/@Name; empty when the document supplied none.

value.description: The value rendered for a human. '(nil)' for xsi:nil, '(reason: text)' for NoValue, '(a, b)' for a structure, '[a, b]' for an array.

overlays.description: Every composed overlay's bin for the last interacted CELL, base first, in the E142Overlays order. Null when the map is not composed. binCode on the payload itself remains the BASE overlay's, unchanged. A layer that says nothing about the cell is LISTED with binCode null rather than omitted - omitting would be ambiguous with 'no such overlay'.

mapVersion.description: Overlay/@MapVersion. With mapName this is OverlayKey, so the pair identifies the overlay.

binCode.description: This overlay's bin code for the cell, or null when it names no bin there.

binQuality.description: The bin's declared quality, or null.

SubstrateMapBinStatistics.title: SubstrateMapBinStatistics
SubstrateMapBinStatistics.description: What readBinStatistics() returns: the whole lattice counted by bin code. UNTRUNCATED, unlike a SubstrateMapGroupSelection histogram, which is capped at ten because an event payload is O(K) in something the document controls and is rebuilt on every tap, and neither is true of a function asked for once per binding. sum(bins[].count) + nullCount === totalCells, exactly and always. A control with nothing bound returns totalCells 0 and an empty list, never null: an empty chart is a state a chart can draw, and null is a state every caller has to branch on.

totalCells.description: Every cell in the lattice, cols * rows. Zero when no map is bound.

nullCount.description: Cells holding the reserved null bin - the map named no code there, or the cell is off the substrate. Counted separately rather than listed as a bin, because the null bin is never painted and a chart that gave it a bar would give it a color it does not have.

bins.description: One entry per code that OCCURS, descending by count then by code. A code declared in BinDefinitions but present in no cell is absent - the list describes the map, not its vocabulary. The order is the one describeGroup uses, so two readings of the same map serialize identically and a chart's bars do not reorder themselves.

count.description: Cells holding it. Never zero - a code with no cells is not listed.

quality.description: The BinQuality the DOCUMENT declared, verbatim, or null when it declared none. The declared token rather than the resolved one, because severity already carries the resolution and this is the only field here that cannot be recovered from the others. E142 reserves Pass and Fail; anything else is a free string and is passed through unchanged.

severity.description: Rank in the declared order, from the same table the aggregate render path uses. Comparable across entries of one reading and meaningless between two maps with different BinSeverityPriority lists.

color.description: The color the RENDER PATH paints for this code, resolved exactly as buildGridPaint resolves it: StatusColorMapping first, then the quality fallback, then the unknown color. Not the raw StatusColorMapping value - a chart built from that disagrees with the map for every code the mapping does not name, and two independent palettes disagreeing is the one failure this function could introduce that nothing else would catch.

SubstrateMapTileSelection.title: SubstrateMapTileSelection
SubstrateMapTileSelection.description: What onSubstrateSelected carries: enough to open the full view on the substrate the operator tapped, and nothing more. NO CELL-LEVEL INFORMATION - the tile is one target and does no hit test, because at 200 px a die is a fraction of a pixel and a coordinate read off one would be a guess dressed as a fact. A dashboard that wants a cell opens the full control. The summary is the same shape readBinStatistics() returns, so a handler that already knows how to read one does not learn a second format.

substrateId.description: The substrate the tile is showing, or null when the bound map declared none. Null rather than an empty string, because 'the map did not say' and 'the map said nothing' are different facts and a dashboard routing on this needs to tell them apart.

lotId.description: The lot, or null when the map declared none. Carried because a dashboard usually opens a lot view rather than a wafer view, and asking the handler to fetch it again would mean a round trip for something already on screen.

state.description: Whether the tile was showing live data or a retained last known state when it was tapped. A handler opening the full view on stale data should say so, and only the tile knows - the id alone cannot tell it. 'demo' and 'nodata' never appear: a tile in those states raises nothing at all.

ageSeconds.description: How old the displayed data was at the moment of the tap, from whichever clock the tile is labeling - the bound MapTimestamp when there is one, the receive time otherwise. Seconds, matching StaleAfterSeconds.

ageSource.description: Which clock ageSeconds came from. 'map' is a bound MapTimestamp; 'received' is when the payload arrived here. The two are different facts - a map that arrived a second ago may describe a wafer tested this morning - so the payload names the source rather than leaving a handler to assume.

goodDevices.description: The DECLARED good-device count, or null when the map declared none. Never recomputed from the bin table: it is what the tester reported, and a number that disagrees with the MES is worse than no number.

summary.description: The aggregate summary, in the shape readBinStatistics() returns. Present even when the tile is showing a retained state, because that is what the operator was looking at.

SubstrateMapChartStyle.title: SubstrateMapChartStyle
SubstrateMapChartStyle.description: Which presentation SubstrateMapBinChart draws. Bars is one bar per category with the count above it; Share is the same data as proportions. One control carries both because they differ only in geometry.

SubstrateMapChartSort.title: SubstrateMapChartSort
SubstrateMapChartSort.description: The category order. CountDescending puts the biggest first, which is what a chart is for. Code orders by the bin code, which is an accident of the sort program's numbering - useful only when two charts must line up. The remainder bucket is last in both.

SubstrateMapSpatialFilter.title: SubstrateMapSpatialFilter
SubstrateMapSpatialFilter.description: Which spatial filter runs over the aggregated tile. The filter works in SCREEN space, after the render and before the blit, with its radius in device pixels - so the result is zoom-dependent by design. This is a fast indicator on a dashboard; it does not replace systematic quality management, and a reproducible geometrically exact tool works from the MES data where there is more than one record. 'Median' takes the most common PALETTE INDEX in the neighborhood, so the answer is always a real bin color - a per-channel median on RGB is forbidden, because the mean of green and red is brown and brown is not a bin category. 'Min' and 'Max' are morphological erosion and dilation over severity rank. 'Box' and 'Gauss' average a scalar field and produce a DENSITY MAP, not a bin map. Each filter requires a compatible FieldView: see SpatialFilterRadius and FieldView.

SubstrateMapFieldView.title: SubstrateMapFieldView
SubstrateMapFieldView.description: Which channel the tile shows, and therefore what a filter would operate on. 'Bins' paints the bin color per pixel and is the categorical view. 'FailDensity' paints the fraction of failing dies per pixel and is a scalar field. 'ValueField' paints a bound relevance map and is also scalar. THE PAIRING MATTERS: Median, Min and Max are categorical and require Bins; Box and Gauss average and require FailDensity or ValueField. An illegal pairing does not filter and reports E142_FILTER_NOT_APPLICABLE naming both values - better to show nothing than to show something wrong.

SubstrateMapReferenceMode.title: SubstrateMapReferenceMode
SubstrateMapReferenceMode.description: How ReferenceGridData is compared against the bound map. 'Off' ignores the reference entirely, so binding one costs nothing until a mode is chosen. 'Difference' shows every cell whose bin differs between the two. 'NewOnly' shows only cells that got WORSE, which is the question an operator asks after a rework step. The reference is an ordinary SubstrateMapGridData and is not re-schema'd for this purpose.

SubstrateMapStatusColorMapping.title: SubstrateMapStatusColorMapping
SubstrateMapStatusColorMapping.description: Maps a status string to a CSS color string. Keys are unconstrained; values are CSS colors.

SubstrateMapGridData.title: SubstrateMapGridData
SubstrateMapGridData.description: The compact, PLC-friendly single-map GridData v1 contract: one substrate, one layout, one bin map, no overlays. Field semantics, enumerations and defaults are SEMI E142 verbatim (V0125 XSD), with one deliberate exception documented on `lowerLeft`. Normalized by the engine's E142Grid.normalizeGridData.

dimension.description: E142 Layout/Dimension: the logical grid extent. Required.

x.description: Number of columns along the layout X axis.

y.description: Number of rows along the layout Y axis.

units.description: E142 Layout/@DefaultUnits: the units every physical field of this document is expressed in (stepSize, deviceSize, lowerLeft). Required. "mm" and "um" are normative; "microns", "<n>Microns" and "mil" are accepted with a warning; anything else is rejected.

stepSize.description: E142 Layout/StepSize: the full pitch (street included), in `units`. Required.

x.description: Column pitch along the layout X axis.

y.description: Row pitch along the layout Y axis.

deviceSize.description: E142 Layout/DeviceSize: the drawn cell extent, in `units`. Optional; defaults to stepSize.

x.description: Drawn cell width along the layout X axis.

y.description: Drawn cell length along the layout Y axis.

lowerLeft.description: Physical anchor: the substrate-frame position of the grid's lower-left corner, in `units`, +y up, origin at the substrate center. Optional; when absent the grid extent is centered on the substrate origin. DELIBERATELY CONTROL-DEFINED: E142's own Layout/LowerLeft is a parent-layout-relative offset and is NOT interchangeable with this field.

x.description: Substrate-frame X of the grid's lower-left corner.

y.description: Substrate-frame Y of the grid's lower-left corner.

orientation.description: E142 SubstrateMap/@Orientation: rotation of the substrate relative to the map data, clockwise-positive. Optional; defaults to 0.

originLocation.description: E142 SubstrateMap/@OriginLocation: the visual cell carrying logical coordinate (0,0). Optional; defaults to "LowerLeft".

axisDirection.description: E142 SubstrateMap/@AxisDirection: the logical axis sign convention. The first token is the Y direction, the second the X direction. Optional; defaults to "UpRight".

binType.description: E142 BinCodeMap/@BinType: the encoding of one bin token. Required. Ascii = 1 printable character; Decimal = 3 digits 000-255, whitespace-separated; HexaDecimal = 2 hex digits; Integer2 = 4 hex digits.

nullBin.description: E142 BinCodeMap/@NullBin: the token standing for "no device / not tested / outside the substrate". Required. Must be a well-formed token of `binType`. Null cells are never painted and never hit.

mapType.description: E142 BinCodeMap/@MapType: the serialization form of `bins`. Optional; defaults to "2DArray" (the standard's prose default - the XSD declares none). "Row/Column" shares "2DArray"'s wire form: GridData carries no run-start field, so a Row/Column map is full-width rows with the cells no run covers written as the NullBin token, and it is decoded as 2DArray.

binDefinitions.description: E142 BinDefinitions/BinDefinition: the per-code metadata. Optional.

binCode.description: The bin token this definition describes. Required.

binQuality.description: Free-form quality string, NOT an enumeration. The conventional values "Pass" and "Fail" get per-quality default colors; every other value falls back to the unknown color unless StatusColorMapping names the code. Defaults to "".

binDescription.description: Human-readable description of the bin. Defaults to "".

binCount.description: Optional running count of devices in this bin.

pick.description: Whether devices of this bin are selected for downstream pick-and-place. Defaults to false.

bins.description: The payload. Its legal form is decided by `mapType`: "Array" takes one token block (string) or one value per cell (number[], row-major); "2DArray" and "Row/Column" take one row per element (string[], top row first, every row the full grid width) or one value per cell (number[], row-major); "Coordinate" takes sparse {x, y, bin} entries whose x/y are logical map coordinates. A number[] is canonicalized to a token per `binType` and must be exactly dimension.x * dimension.y long.

oneOf.description: One continuous token block, row-major starting at the top left (mapType "Array").
One row per element, visual top row first, tokens left to right (mapType "2DArray").
One numeric value per cell, row-major, dimension.x * dimension.y long; each value is canonicalized to a token per `binType`.
Sparse entries, one per addressed device (mapType "Coordinate" only). Cells named by no entry stay NullBin.

x.description: Logical X of the addressed device (may be negative).

y.description: Logical Y of the addressed device (may be negative).

bin.description: The device's bin: the wire token, or its numeric value. Every entry of one payload must use the same form.

lids.description: Optional per-cell location identifiers, mirroring E142 BinCode/@LID. ROW-MAJOR in the same order as the decoded cells (index = row * dimension.x + column, top row first), and exactly dimension.x * dimension.y long - one slot per cell regardless of which form `bins` takes, so there is no shape to match. Use null for a cell the document does not name; an EMPTY STRING is not the same thing - E142 permits a LID of zero length (LID is xs:string with no minLength) and it is retained as given. A LID names the LOCATION, not the device in it: E142 13.4 - 'A location identifier is distinct from the DeviceId ... The location identifier is still present when the device is removed.' Values are opaque: not ordered, not unique by declaration, and never normalized (no trimming, no case folding), because a LID is a join key.

items.description: E142 BinCode/@LID for this cell, or null when the document names no location here.

substrateId.description: E142 Substrate/@SubstrateId. Optional; passed through unchanged to the read-only outputs.

lotId.description: E142 Substrate/LotId. Optional; passed through unchanged to the read-only outputs.

goodDevices.description: E142 Substrate/GoodDevices. Optional; passed through unchanged to the read-only outputs.

SubstrateMapOutlinePreset.title: SubstrateMapOutlinePreset
SubstrateMapOutlinePreset.description: Built-in SEMI substrate outline preset key. "none" selects no preset (a bound Outline or the demo is used instead). All other keys are the built-in SEMI substrate presets.

SubstrateMapE142TransferData.title: SubstrateMapE142TransferData
SubstrateMapE142TransferData.description: SEMI E142.4 (Stream-21) reassembled item content bound at the HMI boundary, in either of two forms: a base64-encoded string (the primary form) or an array of byte values 0..255 (the secondary, PLC-array-friendly form - a BYTE/USINT array marshalled straight through). The bytes are the complete E142.1 MapData XML document, per [E142.04-RQ-00008-00] and [E142.04-RQ-00009-00]; they are decoded to text by the engine's encoding sniff (BOM / XML declaration, UTF-8 default) and then parsed by the same E142Xml pipeline as E142MapData. Stream-21 reassembly (ITEMPART chunking / ordering / acknowledgement) is the host SECS/GEM stack's job and is not represented here. Unset (null) unbinds the input.

oneOf.description: Base64 encoding of the reassembled item bytes.
The reassembled item bytes as an array of byte values.

SubstrateMapAliasIdList.title: SubstrateMapAliasIdList
SubstrateMapAliasIdList.description: The alternate identifiers of the active map's substrate, mirrored from E142 Substrate/AliasIds. Read-only output; null rather than an empty array when the source document carried no AliasIds element, because 'no aliases were stated' and 'an empty list of aliases' are different claims and the E142 schema can only express the first (an empty <AliasIds/> is invalid - AliasIdsType requires at least one AliasId).

type.description: The kind of identifier, from AliasId/@Type. An OPEN vocabulary: E142-0225 Table 7 gives examples ('FrontsideId', 'BacksideId', 'WaferId', 'FrameId') and declares no enumeration, so an unrecognized type is carried verbatim and must not be treated as an error.

value.description: The identifier itself, from AliasId/@Value. Typed MaterialIdType in the E142 schema, hence maxLength 32. Table 7 states the range as 'Text 1-32 characters', but MaterialIdType declares no minLength, so a document may legally carry an empty value; the parser warns and carries it rather than rejecting, and it appears here as an empty string.

SubstrateMapOverlayList.title: SubstrateMapOverlayList
SubstrateMapOverlayList.description: An ordered list of the E142 overlays to compose, one base plus any number of decorations. THE ORDER IS YOURS, not the document's: OverlayKey is (MapName, MapVersion), a set rather than a sequence, so E142 declares no z-order and one must not be inferred from element order. Decorations draw in list order, after the grid and before the origin marker. Null - not an empty array - selects today's single-overlay behavior via E142OverlayName / E142OverlayVersion; those two are ignored with a warning when this list is bound, because a document cannot have two answers to 'which overlay renders'.

name.description: Overlay/@MapName. Required - it is half of OverlayKey and there is no default. Table 9 gives the intended examples: 'CellStatus', 'DefectCode', 'MarkGrade', 'PackageGrade', 'SortGrade', 'DeviceId', 'Transfer' - parallel judgements about the same die, which is why several may be shown at once.

version.description: Overlay/@MapVersion. OMIT to match any version and warn if several exist; supply it to pin one. The EMPTY STRING is not the same as omitting: MapVersion has an XSD default of "", so version:"" selects overlays that state no version, while an absent key does not filter on version at all. R2-1.2's lifecycle - the same MapName downloaded as version 1 and uploaded as version 2 - is exactly why this must be pinnable.

role.description: 'base' owns the geometry, the selection and the bin codes a tap reports; 'decoration' contributes per-cell marks only; 'valueField' REPLACES the fill with a lightness-ordered ramp over that overlay's own BinDefinitions, in document order. Exactly one entry may be 'base' and at most one 'valueField'. A value field is for a per-cell measurement the bin palette cannot express - an LRP relevance map, a thermal field, a probe result - carried as an ordinary E142 overlay whose MapName describes its purpose, exactly as Table 9 intends. It replaces rather than blends for the same reason decorations never take a fill: blending two bin colors yields a color that maps back to no bin code at all. If no entry states a role, the FIRST is the base and the rest are decorations - the common case written the short way. See ws/notes/DECISION-overlay-composition.md for why decorations never take a fill: blending two bin colors produces a color that maps back to no bin code at all.

SubstrateMapAggregationMode.title: SubstrateMapAggregationMode
SubstrateMapAggregationMode.description: Which reduction produced the frame last drawn. 'None' means a cell covers at least one device pixel and is drawn in its own right. 'PointSample' means cells are smaller than a pixel and the renderer paints one cell per pixel, so other cells in that pixel are invisible and which one survives depends on subpixel phase - a defect being reported, not a feature. 'MaxSeverity' and 'FailFraction' name the reducer once aggregation is wired in.

SubstrateMapAggregationReducer.title: SubstrateMapAggregationReducer
SubstrateMapAggregationReducer.description: Which reduction an aggregated tile uses. 'Auto' measures each frame's saturation - the fraction of painted pixels holding at least one failing die - and selects the reducer for the next frame, switching to FailFraction above 0.6 and back below 0.4. 'MaxSeverity' never hides a lone defect; 'FailFraction' never floods a noisy wafer. Force one when the view must not change under the operator.

SubstrateMapBinQualityAliases.title: SubstrateMapBinQualityAliases
SubstrateMapBinQualityAliases.description: Maps an author-defined BinQuality token onto one of the two values SEMI E142-0225 reserves. The standard reserves only 'Pass' and 'Fail' and states that other values are defined by an application, so a document may legally carry any token; this is where the author says what theirs mean. Keys are matched case-insensitively and trimmed. A value that is not 'pass' or 'fail' is ignored.

SubstrateMapBinSeverityPriority.title: SubstrateMapBinSeverityPriority
SubstrateMapBinSeverityPriority.description: Bin codes in severity order, MOST SEVERE FIRST. Orders the bins the ladder cannot distinguish - it knows pass, fail and unknown, and nothing finer. A code the document gives a BinQuality resolving to 'pass' is NEVER promoted by this list and the control warns: the list is most-severe-first, so writing out a whole vocabulary would otherwise put the passing code at the top and let a tile holding one passing and one failing die reduce to the passing bin. A code not present in the bound map is reported and ignored.

SubstrateMapViewTransform.title: SubstrateMapViewTransform
SubstrateMapViewTransform.description: An affine transform as the six components [a, b, c, d, e, f], POST-multiplied onto the world matrix. Null is identity. GEOMETRY ONLY: it moves, scales, rotates, shears or mirrors what is drawn, and cannot express a per-cell value - for a measurement per die, carry it as an E142 overlay and give it the valueField role instead. Six numbers rather than a DOMMatrix because an HMI attribute is JSON; the control builds the matrix. Because it is post-multiplied, e and f are in MILLIMETERS of the substrate frame, not in pixels, and scaling is anchored at the canvas center. Read MapScale to convert: millimeters = pixels / MapScale. A transform with zero determinant is refused with E142_VIEW_TRANSFORM_DEGENERATE and identity is used, because a collapsed matrix draws nothing and would look like a data fault.

SubstrateMapE142MapDataJson.description:
The SEMI E142.1 MapData document as JSON - one more input and output encoding for the engine's E142Document, not a second data model. Member names are the XSD's element and attribute names verbatim, PascalCase; GridData's are camelCase, and that case difference is the boundary between the two vocabularies. See Schema/E142/JSON-FORMAT.md, which is the contract this file encodes.

NOTE ON STRICTNESS: additionalProperties is false throughout, while parseE142Json warns about an unknown member and parses on. That is deliberate and matches GridData: the schema is the engineering-time contract and may be strict, the runtime parser reads other producers' documents and may never be stricter than the schema.

$format.description: Mandatory discriminator, and the FIRST member. A document whose first member is anything else is not an E142 JSON document. No GridData key is named $format, so the two are distinguishable without parsing either further.

$version.description: Mandatory. Versions THIS envelope, not SEMI's schema - that travels in $namespace. 1 is the token form; 2 adds the optional $binary payload member. A document should declare the LOWEST version whose features it uses, so a version-1 reader is not refused a document it could read.

$namespace.description: The E142.1 namespace URI verbatim, so a round trip reproduces it instead of promoting every document to V0125. Absent means the serializer default.
